chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from his father, from Saʿdān, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: "Afflictions are gifts from Allah, and poverty is a stored treasure with Allah."

key_terms.الْمَصَائِبُ: afflictions, hardships, and trials that befall a person
key_terms.عِنْدَ اللَّهِ: with Allah, in the divine presence and keeping
key_terms.مَخْزُونٌ: stored up, reserved, or kept as a treasure
key_terms.مِنَحٌ: gifts or bestowals granted by Allah

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام describe afflictions and poverty?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that afflictions are not merely hardships, but divine gifts carrying spiritual benefit. It also presents poverty, when borne rightly, as something treasured with Allah, pointing to its hidden worth and reward.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Sa’dan who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The difficulties are a Conferment from Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and the poverty is a Hoarded treasure in the Presence of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from Sa’dan who has said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘Misfortunes are gifts from Allah and poverty is in His treasure.’”
